title: Chapter 17: Concurrency and Asynchronous Programming
description: Reason about concurrency from ownership and happens-before guarantees. Learners reproduce races, separate atomicity from visibility, guard invariants with the appropriate primitive, propagate interruption and cancellation, compose CompletableFuture stages on controlled executors, use virtual threads for suitable blocking workloads, bound queues, and shut every executor down deliberately.

lessons.title: Threads, shared memory, races, visibility, and happens-before

exercises.title: Threads, shared memory, races, visibility, and happens-before: concept check
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Does Thread.sleep publish shared writes reliably?
choices: Yes; all caches flush during sleep
Yes; a longer sleep proves safety
No; sleeping is not a synchronization relationship
hints: Recall which actions establish happens-before edges (start, join, monitor release/acquire, volatile write/read) and notice sleep's absence from that list.

lessons.title: synchronized, volatile, locks, conditions, and atomics

exercises.title: synchronized, volatile, locks, conditions, and atomics: concept check
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Thread 1 locks accountA then waits for accountB; Thread 2 locks accountB then waits for accountA. What is the risk, and what practice from this lesson avoids it?
choices: No risk; ReentrantLock detects and prevents this automatically
Deadlock is possible; avoid it by always acquiring the two locks in the same consistent order
The threads will simply queue in the order they called lock()
hints: Picture Thread 1 holding accountA while it waits for accountB at the exact moment Thread 2 holds accountB while waiting for accountA.

lessons.title: Executors, Callable, Future, interruption, cancellation, and shutdown

exercises.title: Executors, Callable, Future, interruption, cancellation, and shutdown: concept check
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Does Future.get(timeout) automatically stop the task on timeout?
choices: No; cancellation and task cooperation need separate handling
Yes; the worker is forcibly killed
Yes; its executor always shuts down
hints: Distinguish what happens to the caller waiting on get from what happens to the still-running task once that wait times out.

exercises.title: CompletableFuture composition, errors, timeouts, and executors: concept check
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Which stage flattens a function returning another future?
hints: Compare a continuation returning a plain value to one returning another CompletableFuture, and ask which combinator avoids a nested future.

lessons.title: Virtual threads, concurrent collections, semaphores, and latches

exercises.title: Virtual threads, concurrent collections, semaphores, and latches: concept check
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Why bound downstream calls when using virtual threads?
choices: Virtual threads remove database pool limits
Cheap waiting threads do not make the downstream service unlimited
hints: Separate the cost of holding a waiting thread from the fixed capacity of the downstream service or connection pool it eventually calls.

exercises.title: Concurrency and Asynchronous Programming: professional judgment
exercises.instructionMarkdown: A task ignores interruption and blocks shutdown. What contract is missing?
choices: Cooperative cancellation and bounded lifecycle management

exercises.title: Join task results without shared mutation
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Implement parallelSum(int[] values). Submit one Callable<Integer> per supplied value to a Java 21 ExecutorService, collect all Future results, and return their sum. Input is non-null, has at most 1000 values, and the sum fits int. Close the executor; on interruption restore the interrupt and throw IllegalStateException with the cause; wrap other task failures with their cause. Automated tests verify results only: review executor ownership, actual submission, and cancellation behavior separately.
hints: Submit one Callable per array element before calling get on any Future, so all tasks are running concurrently rather than sequentially.
On InterruptedException, restore the interrupt with Thread.currentThread().interrupt() and wrap it in IllegalStateException; unwrap other Future failures' causes before rethrowing.

exercises.title: Restore interruption
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Repair the supplied defect so the program writes exactly `true`. The catch block currently swallows InterruptedException without restoring the interrupted status; preserve the surrounding try/catch structure while making the thread's interrupted flag observable again, and explain why your fix changes the result instead of hard-coding the print. Output tests verify the printed result; preserving the intended interruption contract requires reading the source, not just matching output.
hints: The catch must restore the interrupted status when it cannot propagate the exception.
